findings.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3785` (`*ast.GrantRoleStmt`) only checks restricted-ness of `raw.Roles` via `appendVisitInfoIsRestrictedUser(...)`, but never checks `raw.Users` (the grantees). In contrast, `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3793` (`*ast.RevokeRoleStmt`) checks `raw.Users`, and `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3756` (`*ast.GrantStmt`) checks `raw.Users`. Executor path `pkg/executor/simple.go:2071` (`executeGrantRole`) performs no restricted-user enforcement and relies on planner `visitInfo`, so missing `raw.Users` checks directly becomes allowed runtime behavior.
findings.fix: In `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` `case *ast.GrantRoleStmt`, add a loop over `raw.Users` and call `appendVisitInfoIsRestrictedUser(ctx, ..., user, "RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN")` (similar to `*ast.RevokeRoleStmt`). Keep the existing `raw.Roles` loop to continue protecting restricted roles.
findings.impact: Privilege boundary bypass under SEM: a user with `SUPER`/`ROLE_ADMIN` but without `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` can still modify a restricted account’s effective privileges by granting roles to it (e.g. `GRANT some_role TO restricted_user`), undermining the intended protection that prevents modifying restricted accounts via `GRANT`/`REVOKE`.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go` still has `*ast.GrantRoleStmt` restricted checks only over `raw.Roles` and not `raw.Users`. No executor-side compensation observed (`upstream/master:pkg/executor/simple.go:2071`).
findings.verify: Extend `pkg/privilege/privileges/privileges_test.go` `TestProtectUserAndRoleWithRestrictedPrivileges` to cover `GRANT <non-restricted role> TO <restricted_user_X>` under SEM (V1+V2): expect failure for a SUPER user lacking `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN`, and success for a user with `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN`.
findings.what: `GRANT ROLE` does not enforce `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` when the *grantee user* is restricted, allowing role assignment to restricted accounts without the required dynamic privilege.

subject: privileges,planner: implement checks for `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` for granting privileges and roles (#64297)
summary: Found a High-severity SEM privilege hole: `GRANT ROLE` enforces `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN` only for restricted *roles* being granted, not for restricted *users* receiving roles, enabling role-based privilege modification of restricted accounts without `RESTRICTED_USER_ADMIN`.
